text: In the second year after Israel’s departure from Egypt—on the twentieth day of the second month—the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.

content:
Today we continue our study from Numbers chapter ten. Yesterday we saw that Israel began their journey from Sinai in the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, and we learned that the second year points to a new stage after redemption. Israel was no longer only a rescued people; they were now a prepared, ordered, taught, and sanctified people, with the Tabernacle in their midst. Today we will look more closely at the second month itself. When we search the Scriptures, we find that many important events happened in the second month, and these events are not random. A beautiful pattern begins to appear. The second month again and again connects with judgment, restoration, provision, preparation, mercy, movement, and the building of the house of God. So, the second month is not just a date on the calendar. It teaches us how Yahweh deals with His people after a major beginning.

The first important event we see in the second month is the beginning of the great flood in the days of Noah. Genesis 7:11 says, "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened." This was the day judgment began upon the old world. The earth had become filled with violence and corruption. Man had turned away from Yahweh, and the thoughts of his heart were continually evil. So Yahweh judged that world by water. But even in the midst of judgment, Yahweh preserved Noah and his family safely inside the ark. Here we see the first lesson of the second month. The old world was judged, but a new world was being prepared. The flood was not only the end of the old world; it was also the beginning of a new stage for Noah and his household.

This gives us a deep lesson for the New Creation. When Yahweh begins His work in us, He must first judge the old man. The old way of life, the old mind, the old desires, the old world within us, must all come under judgment. We cannot carry the old habits into the new creation life. As Paul says, "Old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new" (2 Corinthians 5:17). The second month therefore teaches us that new life begins with the judgment of the old. Before Yahweh brings us into a new world, He separates us from the old one. Just as Noah entered the ark, we enter into Christ, and in Him we are preserved while the old world passes away.

The next event in the second month is also connected with Noah, and it is very beautiful. Genesis 8:14 says, "And in the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dried." Think of it. The flood began in the second month, and the earth was made ready again in the second month. The same month that saw judgment also saw restoration. Yahweh did not only judge the old world;
He also prepared the earth for a new beginning. This shows us that God’s judgment is never without purpose. When He removes the old, it is because He is preparing something new. When He dries the earth, He is making a place for renewed life.Noah and his family came out of the ark into a cleansed world, ready for a fresh beginning before God. For the New Creation, this teaches us that the Almighty God does not only expose and remove our old life; He also restores us. He does not leave us empty after judgment. He prepares our hearts to become fruitful again. Sometimes He must dry up the floodwaters in our lives, removing confusion, fear, and instability, and then He gives us firm ground to stand upon.

The next important second-month event is found in Exodus 16:1, which says, "And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt." This happened shortly after Israel came out of Egypt. They had crossed the Red Sea and seen Yahweh's mighty hand. But now they entered the wilderness, and the people began to complain because of food. They remembered the food of Egypt and spoke against Moses and Aaron. Yet Yahweh did not abandon them. In the second month, He began to feed His redeemed people with manna from heaven. This is a beautiful lesson for the New Creation. After we are delivered from Egypt, we quickly learn that the wilderness cannot feed us. The world cannot sustain the new life God has given us. Egypt's food may satisfy the flesh for a time, but it can never nourish the spirit. So God gives bread from heaven. In the New Testament, Christ reveals the true meaning of this when He says, "I am the bread of life" (John 6:35). The manna pointed to Christ, the true bread who came down from heaven. Just as Israel had to gather manna daily, so the New Creation must feed daily upon Christ through the Word of God. After redemption, God provides spiritual food. He does not bring us out of Egypt and leave us hungry; He feeds us with Christ and teaches us to depend on Him day by day.

The next event connected with the second month is the building of the Temple in the days of Solomon. In 1 Kings 6:37 we read, "In the fourth year was the foundation of the house of Yahweh laid, in the month Zif." The month Zif, also called Ziv, is the second month. And 2 Chronicles 3:2 tells us that Solomon began to build on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign. So the foundation of the house of Yahweh was laid in the second month. This is very important, for it shows us that the second month is not only connected with judgment and provision, but also with the building of Yahweh's house. For Israel, this was the beginning of a great work.
The Temple was to be the place where Yahweh's name would dwell, the centre of worship, sacrifice, prayer, and fellowship. The foundation had to be laid before the house could be completed. For the New Creation, this connects beautifully with who we are in Christ. We are not a physical temple made with stones. We are the spiritual house of God. Peter says, "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house"(1 Peter 2:5), and Paul says that we are "builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Ephesians 2:22). So the second month teaches us that God is building His house. After He delivers us, feeds us, and restores us, He begins to build. He lays the foundation of truth in our hearts, He places Christ as the chief cornerstone, He joins living stones together, and He shapes us and fits us into His spiritual Temple. This reminds us that the New Creation is not an individual journey only. We are being built together. God’s purpose is not merely to save separate people, but to build a dwelling place for Himself through the Spirit.

The next event is Hezekiah's Passover, also kept in the second month. 2 Chronicles 30:2 says, "For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the Passover in the second month." Many of the priests and people were not ready in the first month. They had not cleansed themselves, and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem. So Hezekiah and the leaders decided to keep the Passover in the second month, and 2 Chronicles 30:15 tells us, "Then they killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month." This event shows us the mercy of God. The people had delayed, and many were not prepared at the normal time. Yet God allowed them to return to true worship and gave them an opportunity to keep the Passover in the second month. This connects with Numbers 9, where God also gave a second Passover for those who were unclean or away on a journey. It shows that God is merciful to those who truly desire to draw near to Him. He does not reject a sincere heart that wants to return. For the New Creation, this is a powerful lesson. Many of us did not understand the truth at the first opportunity. Many of us were delayed by tradition, by uncleanness, by confusion, by wrong teaching, or by spiritual distance. But Yahweh in His mercy called us again. He opened another door and restored us to true worship. The second month therefore speaks of mercy and restoration. It teaches us that God calls His people back when they have delayed and restores worship when it has been neglected. But this mercy should not make us careless. It should make us thankful. If God has given us another opportunity to return to truth, we must not waste it. We must cleanse ourselves, come before Him with sincerity, and keep the feast in spirit and in truth.

Now when we place all these second-month events together, the pattern becomes clear and beautiful. In the second month, the old world was judged in Noah's day. In the second month, the earth was dried and prepared for a new beginning. In the second month, Israel received manna from heaven. In the second month, the foundation of Solomon's Temple was laid. In the second month, Hezekiah restored the Passover for those who were not ready in the first month. In the second month, Zerubbabel began rebuilding the Temple after the return from Babylon. And in Numbers chapter ten, in the second month, the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle and Israel began to move forward. So the second month carries a beautiful spiritual message. It speaks of the judgment of the old, the restoration of the new, the provision of bread from heaven, the building of the house of God, mercy for those who return, and movement after preparation.

For the New Creation, the lesson is clear and full of hope. Yahweh has brought us out of Egypt. He has judged the old life. He has given us Christ, the true bread from heaven. He is building us together as His spiritual Temple. He has shown us mercy when we were delayed and unclean. He is rebuilding what captivity destroyed. And when His preparation is complete, He lifts the cloud and leads us forward. Therefore we must respond faithfully. We must leave the old world behind. We must feed daily on the bread from heaven. We must allow God to build His house in us. We must return to true worship with thankful hearts. We must help in the rebuilding work. And when the cloud moves, we must be ready to follow. The second month teaches us that God is not finished with His people after deliverance. He restores, He feeds, He builds, and He moves them forward. This is the journey of the New Creation. Tomorrow, God willing, we will study the meaning of the twentieth day.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We marvel at how carefully You have woven Your purpose through every season.

In the same month You judged the old world and dried the earth for a new beginning.

In the same month You fed Your people with bread from heaven and laid the foundation of Your house.

In the same month You showed mercy to those who came late, and began to rebuild what was broken.

Do this same work in us; purge our old life, feed us with Christ, and build us as living stones.

And when Your preparation is complete and the cloud lifts, make us ready to follow.

"Great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised; and His greatness is unsearchable."

In the name of Christ, the foundation and cornerstone of Your house, we pray. Amen.
